lemma: Balanced-node lemma. For every full binary vtree T with m >= 2 leaves, there is a non-root node v (a leaf or an internal node other than the root) with m/3 < leaves(v) <= 2m/3.
gap: The lemma gives a balanced cut but does NOT close G0001. Still open: a lower bound on max over the balanced cut's signature size log2|Sigma| for a cubic expander, for every vtree that the balanced node induces. The cut-rank-to-DNNF step and any uniform rank bound across the balanced cut are not proved. Linear-vtree data (cm-01641bcf3d8b4fd4) cannot supply that bound.
evidence: cm-f5ee9146624f4bec (balanced-node check m=2..10, all_pass true); cm-cf6d8fcd311641e9 is superseded (it omitted leaf nodes and gave a false FAIL at m=2).
proved_step: PROOF. Let S be the set of non-root internal nodes v with leaves(v) > 2m/3. Case 1: S is empty. The root's two children each have at most 2m/3 leaves and sum to m, so the larger child c has leaves(c) >= m/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Case 2: S is nonempty. Choose v in S with no descendant in S (deepest). Both children of v have at most 2m/3 leaves, and they sum to leaves(v) > 2m/3. The larger child c has leaves(c) >= leaves(v)/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Both cases give 3*leaves(v) in (m, 2m]. Finite check: exhaustive over all binary tree shapes for m = 2..10 (cm-f5ee9146624f4bec, 0 failures; counts 1,2,5,14,42,132,429,1430,4862). INDEPENDENCE NOTE: the check is by enumeration of the same shapes the proof covers, so it guards only against boundary/off-by-one errors. The proof itself is the argument above. Status: CLAIMED; needs independent review.

proved_step: RANK IDENTITY (LEMMA, CLAIMED; closes no obligation). Setting: finite graph G=(V,E) with no isolated vertices; E is a disjoint union A u B; d = {v : deg_A(v)>0 and deg_B(v)>0}. For a subset a of A, call a VALID iff every vertex with deg_B(v)=0 is covered exactly once by a and every vertex covered by a at most once; sigma(a) in {0,1}^d with sigma(a)_v = number of a-edges at v. Define b, tau(b) symmetrically. Let f(a,b)=1 iff a u b is a perfect matching of G. CLAIM: f(a,b) = [a valid][b valid][sigma(a)_v + tau(b)_v = 1 for all v in d]. Hence for every field F, rank_F M_{A,B} = number of signatures sigma realised by a valid a for which some valid b has tau(b) = 1 - sigma (compatible signatures). PROOF: (1) If a u b is a PM, restricting to A and B gives valid a, b, and each boundary vertex is covered once in total, split between A and B, so the sum condition holds. Conversely, valid a, b with the sum condition cover every vertex exactly once. (2) So M[a,b] depends only on (sigma(a), tau(b)). Rows with equal sigma are equal. (3) Nonzero entries occur only between row class sigma and column class 1-sigma; distinct sigma give disjoint row sets and disjoint column sets. So M is, up to permutation, a direct sum of all-ones blocks R_sigma x C_{1-sigma} over compatible sigma, plus zero rows and columns. (4) Each all-ones block has rank 1 over every field, and direct sums add ranks. SCOPE: an identity only. It gives no lower bound by itself; G0001 (all-vtree lower bound on max_node log2|Sigma_node| for an explicit cubic expander family) remains OPEN. Same model family as the author (haiku): needs independent review from another family before any use as a premise.
